_why: THE SHAPE OF AN ANCHOR, as data rather than as source.
It lived in $script:AnchorFields inside anchor.ps1, which made it a policy literal in
code: PLAN A.2 forbids that, and it also meant only PowerShell could ever ask what an
anchor is. The org needs more readers than that - the harness, the sessions bridge, and
later agent-bridge - so the definition moves here and the readers become thin.
TWO MODES, ONE OBJECT (ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN 6.6, adopted by dark-factory-unification L1).
agent-org already split convergence into generative discovery and adversarial hardening;
the harness's anchor was only ever the second kind. They are one concept with a mode
field, not two systems:
mode B - bounded work. A hard target with stated failure conditions. Approaches zero;
completion is diminishing returns across DIVERSE lenses. This is every anchor
the harness has ever taken, so B is the default and its contract is unchanged.
mode A - generative discovery. The North Star is the original prompt, and it is a THEME,
not a spec: the goal comes into focus by walking the path. Off-theme ideas
become constraints that narrow it, never tasks. Zero propagation here is a red
flag, not success.
WHY MODE A FORBIDS AN ACCEPTANCE LIST. Not tidiness - gym-024 is the recorded cost. A
complete, D2-passing PR read as 'unconverged' because a fixed-target reading was applied
to a generative loop. 6.6 is explicit that no fixed acceptance list can exist for Mode A,
so an anchor carrying one is a category error the schema refuses rather than a style
preference it tolerates.
COMPATIBILITY. Anchors written before this file have no `mode` field. Absent means B, so
every anchor already in the queue stays valid - this is an extension, not a migration.

rules.min_acceptance_criterion_why: an acceptance criterion nobody can check is a wish; this catches the common shape - a single vague line - without pretending to judge English

B.desc: bounded work: a fixed target with stated failure conditions

goal.why: one sentence, the outcome in the operator's words - what stops goal drift across test cycles

artifact.why: the path and kind of the thing that will exist - 'a README' vs 'a report' is a decision, not a style

audience.why: who reads or runs it - the field that would have prevented the coder README

acceptance.why: objectively checkable criteria - this is what the tester tests against

out_of_scope.why: explicit non-goals - where 'and also fix what you find' gets refused

findings_sink.why: where incidental discoveries go, so real findings are neither lost nor pasted into the deliverable. Its contents are held to the SAME standard as the artifact - a claim about what a script does is verified against that code path, not against its comments

A.desc: generative discovery: a theme walked toward, not a spec exhausted

north_star.why: the original prompt, kept verbatim - every round realigns against THIS, not against a re-derived scope goal, whose drift produces a meaningless count

audience.why: who the work is found toward - gym-035 ran ~13 hours on packaging metadata and linting config because nothing asked whether the work served a North Star phrased for a real person

constraints.why: the standing constraint ledger, seeded here and grown by the loop: an off-theme idea becomes a clause that narrows the path ('the way to this goal does not run here'), never a task and never a silent drop

out_of_scope.why: directions ruled out up front - the same refusal as mode B, but advisory here because Mode A expects the boundary to sharpen as the path is walked

findings_sink.why: as mode B - true-but-elsewhere goes here, held to the artifact's standard

forbidden.acceptance: mode A cannot carry a fixed acceptance list (ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN 6.6): the goal comes into focus by walking the path, so a list written up front is a target that does not exist yet. gym-024 read a delivered, D2-passing product as unconverged for exactly this conflation. Use mode B if the work really does have a fixed target.
